title: Winter Hours
price_note: On sale December 10 at independent newsagents in Corran, or by post
summary: The longest nights of the year: the snow crews, the shelter volunteers, the people who keep the lights on in December. Members read two stories early.
letter:
Winter is the season night workers talk about most. Not because it is harder, though it is, but because it is the only time of year the rest of the city notices them.

This issue is still at the printer. Members can read two of its stories now, in the back room.

title: The Early Shift
price_note: Available at independent newsagents in Corran, or by post
summary: Bakers, porters and the people whose night ends when yours begins. The companion issue to season two of the podcast.
letter:
Every episode of the podcast this season starts with a clock: the time the guest's shift begins. This issue does the same.

Dellah Morrow is on the cover because her shift starts at one, which made her the only person we could photograph in the dark and the dawn on the same night.

title: Summer Nights
price_note: A few copies left at the office; members can read the whole issue online
summary: Short nights and long shifts: the milkman, the taxi rank and the people who work through the shortest night of the year.
letter: Midsummer gives a night worker about six hours of dark. We spent the shortest night of the year with five of them.

title: The Late Issue
price_note: Sold out; members can read the whole issue online
summary: Our first issue with the podcast: press rooms, night buses and the late edition.
letter: The first issue of Halflight came out a week late. We decided that was the point.
